predecessors.name: Crown of Aragon
predecessors.text: the Balearic Islands and the mainland counties of Roussillon and Cerdanya, held by the Crown of Aragon before 1276

successors.name: Crown of Aragon
successors.text: the Balearic Islands, Roussillon and Cerdanya, invaded by Peter IV in 1343 and 1344

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: James III's 'French possessions', sold to the King of France in 1349

ledger.x: 1276: James II takes the Kingdom of Majorca, the Balearic Islands with Roussillon, Cerdanya and Montpellier.
1295: the Treaty of Anagni returns the Balearic Islands to James II of Majorca.
1305: Menorca appears in the Kingdom's outline (Cliopatria's 1305 shape adds two cells there).
1343: Peter IV of Aragon invades the Balearic Islands.
1343: the Balearic Islands pass to Aragon.
1344: Peter IV invades Roussillon and Cerdanya.
1344: the fighting over the three zones is treated as over on the mainland invasion year.
1349: James III sells his French possessions to the King of France.
1349: James III is killed at Llucmajor and the Kingdom of Majorca ends in personal union with Aragon.

wars.name: Aragonese conquest of Mallorca
wars.outcome: Alfonso of Aragon conquered Mallorca in 1286; the Treaty of Anagni of 20 June 1295 provided for the restitution of the Balearic Islands to James II of Majorca.

wars.name: Conquest of Majorca by Peter IV of Aragon
wars.outcome: Peter IV conquered the Balearic Islands (May 1343) and Roussillon and Cerdanya (1344); James III was defeated and killed at Llucmajor on 25 October 1349 and the kingdom stayed in personal union with Aragon.

certainty.note: The island coasts are natural lines, but the Pyrenean frontier of Roussillon and Cerdanya and the Montpellier lordship are approximate; no treaty in the pages fixes a boundary.
